subject: fringe-lipped bat
title: This Bat Hunts Frogs by Their Love Songs, and Knows Which Are Poison

scenes.text: This bat finds its dinner by listening to love songs.
In Panama's rainforest, male frogs call all night to attract females.
The fringe-lipped bat is eavesdropping. It homes in on the call and grabs the singer.
But some of those calls come from toxic toads. Adult bats barely react to them.
Young bats do. A 2025 study found juveniles go after toxic calls that adults ignore.
So every bat has to learn the playlist: which song is dinner, and which one is poison.

description:
The fringe-lipped bat of Central and South America hunts frogs by eavesdropping on the calls males use to attract mates.
Adult bats largely ignore the calls of toxic toads and of frogs too big to carry. A 2025 study from the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute in Panama, published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B, found that juvenile bats respond to those toxic calls far more than adults do, so the skill is learned with experience.
Which would you rather be: the frog that sings, or the one that stays quiet? Comment below.
first_comment: Adult bats remember specific frog calls year after year. If singing got you eaten, would you still sing?
